newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Sophus up on restructure talk.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Sophus up on restructure talk.

text.p: Danish holding company Sophus Berendsen, main shareholder in Britain's Rentokil, rose by 3.4 percent on Wednesday on the Copenhagen stock exchange after a newspaper reported that it planned to concentrate its 37.5 percent Rentokil holding in a separately-listed company.

At 1015 GMT the share was up 28 crowns, to 846, its highest level so far this year. It has risen by about 12 percent over the past week, fuelled by analysts' recommendations and talk of restructuring.
"Even though it's a bit of an old story...the market has reacted very positively," a dealer said.
Sophus executives could not immediately be reached for comment.
Rentokil contributed 533 million crowns to Sophus Berendsen's 640 million crown first-half 1996 earnings.

The group has sought to stress the earnings of its other holdings but last November admitted that losses in its Electronics and Data division meant that full-year non-Rentokil profits were likely to fall to 145 million crowns from 1995's 275 million.
